subject: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan

Team —

Quick background: our contracts for product & API analytics are coming up over the next 4 months and we need a coordinated plan. Key expiries: Amplitude (Mar 15), Segment (Apr 1), Mixpanel (May 1). We currently split collection between Segment (server-side API), Mixpanel (product events), and Amplitude (user engagement dashboards).

Ask: can we put together a short recommendation + numbers to present to procurement and legal next week? Goal is to either:
- Consolidate to one primary product analytics vendor for product & API events, or
- Keep a two-vendor posture with explicit split and cost/retention tradeoffs.

Please capture: current monthly event volume, estimated uplift if we keep both Segment and Amplitude, retention/residency needs, query costs for Mixpanel, and any upcoming product launches that will materially increase traffic. I attached the last two invoices and our current instrumentation guide for reference.

Initial timeline: internal recommendation by Jan 20, procurement negotiation Jan 21–28, legal review the week of Feb 2.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync for Jan 15 to go over numbers.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: invoices_2025_q4.zip (summary), instrumentation_playbook_v2.pdf

From: alex.porter@amplitude.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marta.ruiz@mixpanel.com, samir@segmentsolutions.co
Date: 2026-01-12T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan

Jonas — thanks for the heads up. Attaching our renewal proposal and a short appendix that shows the projected cost at current event volumes and for a 30% growth scenario. We can be flexible on retention tiers and are willing to offer an onboarding credit if you consolidate more workloads to Amplitude.

Two quick questions that will help price things:
- Can you share current monthly API event counts (server-side) and mobile/web event counts separately?
- Any contractual constraints on EU residency for analytics data?

We’re happy to join the Jan 15 sync — I’ll bring our product specialist and CSM.

Best,
Alex Porter
Enterprise Account Exec, Amplitude
Attachments: Amplitude_Renewal_Proposal_Q1_2026.pdf, Amplitude_pricing_appendix.csv

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-14T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan

Circling back with the numbers Jonas asked for — pulled from Snowflake and our pipeline:
- Server-side (API) events: 45M events / month (currently routed through Segment)
- Client-side (web + mobile) events: 22M events / month (mix: Mixpanel and Amplitude)
- 90-day retention hot table size: ~2.1TB (mostly product events used by experiments)

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Segment: cheap for routing, but adds latency and costs for heavy server-side payloads. Migration off Segment would reduce TTM for some infra work but requires engineering cycles to change SDKs and webhooks.
- Amplitude: stronger product backfills and experiment-friendly pipelines + cohorts; query costs less of an issue for our main dashboards. Amplitude asked for a consolidation credit which could make the unit economics favorable.
- Mixpanel: good for ad-hoc event cohorting but query costs for large historical scans are higher; they'd charge more to expand retention beyond current tier.

Recommendation (short): pursue a consolidation-to-Amplitude pilot for product + API events for the next 3 months while negotiating renewal terms with Segment and Mixpanel. Capture a rollback plan and keep a minimal Segment routing layer for edge cases.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_example_playbook — I added an event taxonomy slice and cost model (tab: "Jan26_cost_model").

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Analytics Lead
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@vendorco.com
Date: 2026-01-19T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan

Thanks team — I ran the vendor quotes against Laura's event model and attached a side-by-side comparison (Segment_Migration_Estimate.xlsx). High level:
- Short term (next 3 months): cheapest path is a 3-month extension with current vendors while we validate the consolidation plan. That gives us leverage to extract consolidation credits from Amplitude and negotiate lower retention overage rates with Mixpanel.
- Mid term (3–12 months): consolidation to Amplitude looks plausible and reduces duplicated storage/ingestion costs by ~18% on our baseline. However, engineering migration cost is estimated at ~0.5 FTE for 6 weeks (mostly infra and QA).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Ask Amplitude for a 90-day bridge contract with the consolidation credit included (Jonas to lead vendor conversation).
2) Request Mixpanel to provide a temporary retention/scan credit while we transition (Marissa to draft request).
3) Legal to put a short playbook together for rollback SLA and data export obligations.

Attached: Segment_Migration_Estimate.xlsx (cost compare), Vendor_Renewal_Playbook_v1.md (draft).

Marissa Cole
Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Segment_Migration_Estimate.xlsx, Vendor_Renewal_Playbook_v1.md

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: alex.porter@amplitude.com, marta.ruiz@mixpanel.com, samir@segmentsolutions.co
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, procurement@vendorco.com
Date: 2026-01-23T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API analytics vendor renewal: cross-vendor evaluation and renewal plan

Alex / Marta / Samir — thanks for the proposals and for joining the internal sync earlier this month. Quick decision from our side based on the internal cost model and migration estimate: we will request a 90-day extension with Amplitude that includes the consolidation/onboarding credit. During that 90-day window we will:
- Kick off a migration pilot to route API events from Segment to Amplitude (engineering lead: k.iyer@redwood.com).
- Keep a lightweight Segment instance for edge-case routing and backfills.
- Ask Mixpanel for a temporary retention credit for historical scans during migration.

Jonas will lead the commercial discussion with Amplitude; Marissa will run a parallel negotiation with Mixpanel and Segment for short-term credits. Legal will prepare the rollback SLA language and data export checklist.

Please confirm availability for a POC kickoff meeting next Wed (Jan 28) at 10am PT. Also Alex, please send the updated 90-day bridge contract and SOW; include the consolidation credit appendix and a brief runbook for the cutover.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — goal is to have the bridge in place before Segment's Apr 1 renewal window opens.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced in thread: Amplitude_Renewal_Proposal_Q1_2026.pdf, Segment_Migration_Estimate.xlsx, Vendor_Renewal_Playbook_v1.md
